title: Using F = ma with several forces
canonical_question: How do you apply F = ma when several forces act on the same body?
summary: When many forces act, first add them as vectors to get the single net force.
A box pushed with 10 N forward while 4 N of friction acts backward feels a net 6 N.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Sum first, then divide
sections.body_md: When many forces act, first add them as vectors to get the single net force. Only that net force goes into F = ma. Then the acceleration is the net force divided by the mass.

sections.heading: A quick case
sections.body_md: A box pushed with 10 N forward while 4 N of friction acts backward feels a net 6 N. If its mass is 2 kg, its acceleration is 3 m/s^2 forward. The trick is always to combine forces before dividing.

key_points: Combine all forces into one net force.
Only the net force enters F = ma.
Then divide by the mass for acceleration.
core.bridge_to_parent: It applies the objective’s law when forces compete.
